commands.name: skill:building-galaxy-mini-apps
commands.description: Build a GalaxyFinX/Vikki Track C web mini app that mounts inside the super-app Host over Module Federation and also runs standalone. Use when creating a new mini app, adding screens or flows to one, wiring the Host runtime contract (theme, auth, HTTP client, navigation), fixing a mini app that will not mount in the Host, repairing a GG Studio sandbox whose Visual Editor Inspect selects nothing or whose preview Back/Forward do nothing (`studio_preview_bridge_unreachable`), or reviewing mini-app architecture. Covers any domain — payments, onboarding, booking, servicing, KYC.

commands.name: skill:calling-other-mini-apps
commands.description: Make one mini app call another one, or a platform capability, through the frontend SDK broker — `MiniApps.invoke` for a headless call, `MiniApps.open` + `__rpcId` + `finish`/`cancel` for a screen, and the provider side that answers them. Use when a screen needs something another mini app owns (OTP, eKYC, payment, device id, keychain, HTTP), when exposing this app so others can call it, when a broker call hangs or reports a capability missing, or when a generated app must keep working standalone in the GG Studio sandbox where the registry is empty. Measured on the installed SDK and on the 17-app `galaxy-g-web-mini-apps` corpus.

commands.name: skill:calling-vikki-system-apis
commands.description: Call the real Vikki system backend from a GG Studio web mini app — the gateway prefix, the GTW-Authorization header, the one response envelope, how to find an app's own endpoints from its legacy route table, how to learn a request body in one round trip, and how to tell a POST that reads from a POST that moves money. Applies to every service behind the gateway, not a fixed catalogue. Use when a screen needs real customer data instead of a fixture, when migrating any legacy mini app, when a call returns 404 "no Route matched" or a 500 that is really a client mistake or a 200 that is actually a failure, or when deciding between a direct client now and sdk.http later.

commands.name: skill:debugging-galaxy-mini-apps
commands.description: Find the real cause of a defect in a generated mini app — a white screen on a route that compiles, a screen that renders while throwing, a total off by a tax nobody asked for, a guard that never refuses, a step that never advances, a call that returns 200 and shows nothing — and prove the fix in the running app rather than in the diff. Use when a turn opens with "The app you just built COMPILES but does not RUN", when the same error survives your fix, when a value on screen disagrees with the spec, when `tsc` and `vite build` are green and the preview is not, and before claiming any defect is fixed. Measured on real builds — 2,053 lines and a clean bundle hid a white screen, and one WebSocket line burned a whole repair turn on a defect never in `src/`.

commands.name: skill:enabling-miniapp-build-modes
commands.description: Make a GG Studio mini app ship all of its build modes — the ordinary Preview build (`dist/`), the single-file Standalone build (`dist-standalone/`, one `index.html` a reviewer double-clicks), the Host (mount) Module Federation manifest, and the Dual-thread engine build — so the Submit dialog's chips are live links instead of muted `· chưa bật` labels. Use when generating a new mini app, when a user asks for standalone/dual-thread/host support on an existing or legacy mini app, when a chip stays `chưa bật` after a submit, when a `standalone/` link opens a blank page, or before claiming a mode is enabled. Every rule here is read off the platform code that decides (`static_build.py`, `host_registry.py`, `submit_steps_router.py`) and was measured on a real build of this platform's own scaffold.

commands.name: skill:enforcing-spec-rules
commands.description: Turn a requirement document's stated rules — a deadline, a formula, a quantity, a set of named states — into code that actually refuses the wrong thing, and verify it by driving the app rather than by reading the diff. Use whenever a BRD, spec, or acceptance-criteria list states a number, a time limit, a total, or a list of statuses; whenever a screen shows a countdown, a price, a counter, or a result badge; and before claiming a requirement is implemented. This is the behavioural counterpart to the screenshot-compare-fix loop — that loop proves a screen LOOKS right, and nothing else in this skill set proves it BEHAVES right.

commands.name: skill:find-skills
commands.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

commands.name: skill:galaxy-app-definition
commands.description: Author a GG Studio App Definition (app-definition/ directory) from a mini app's real source code, so the Studio's Visual, Layout and Journey editors can render the app structurally. Read this after writing or changing screen code.

commands.name: skill:galaxy-core-ui
commands.description: Build UI with the GalaxyFinX Core UI design system (@galaxyfinx/galaxy-g-core-ui-web) so screens look native to the platform and survive every brand and theme. Use when writing or reviewing any screen, component, or styling for a GalaxyFinX host app or mini app (Vikki, HDBank, VietJet Air, Smile Living), when choosing which Core UI component to use, when a screen must work for more than one brand, or when a design looks hand-built instead of systemic. Also use before building a result, receipt, success, processing or failure screen — the platform's status mark is ReceiptCard's animated icon/confetti/logo slots, not Icon name="success", and a static design frame is not evidence against motion — and whenever a story's snippet passes an image path a turn is about to copy verbatim.

commands.name: skill:galaxy-frontend-sdk
commands.description: Call other mini apps and platform capabilities from a GalaxyFinX/Vikki mini app via the frontend SDK broker (@galaxyfinx/galaxy-g-frontend-sdk) and the HTTP client (@galaxyfinx/galaxy-g-http-client). Use when a mini app needs payment, eKYC, keychain, device id, or any capability another mini app or the Host provides, when wiring inter-mini-app calls, or when deciding whether an SDK feature works in a web Module Federation remote at all.

commands.name: skill:galaxy-miniapp-reference
commands.description: Real, verbatim reference source from `flight-booking-1` (the current gold-standard GG Studio-generated mini app) for the patterns a rule alone cannot teach — a real two-column responsive shell, a real sticky action bar, real measured breakpoints. Use when building a multi-step flow, a detail-plus-sidebar screen, or any screen that must behave correctly at both desktop and a real 390px phone width. Complements `building-galaxy-mini-apps` (rules) and `galaxy-core-ui` (component choice) — this skill is examples, not rules.

commands.name: skill:generating-miniapp-screens
commands.description: The ORDER a screen is generated in, and the reasoning at each step — inventory the design, derive the grid from the design system's own constants, place regions, pick components, wire mock data with real latency, then states, then colour and assets, then hover/motion, and measure after every step. Use when generating a new mini app or a new screen from any design source, when a generated screen compiles but looks hand-built or "almost right", when deciding what to build first, or when a fix keeps moving the layout instead of settling it.

commands.name: skill:handling-claude-design
commands.description: Read, drive, and describe a Claude Design export (a `*.dc.html` document plus its `_ds/`, `assets/`, `uploads/` siblings) cheaply and correctly when building a mini app from one. Use when a project's design source is a Claude Design export, when deciding what screens or variants it has, what a screen actually looks like, which design-system components map onto Core UI, or how to open one exact screen in a browser that has no click-through navigation to it.

commands.name: skill:handling-figma-design
commands.description: Build a GG Studio screen from a pasted Figma link using this repo's own Figma MCP integration (agent-service/app/mcp, doc 70) — the real, wired tool surface (get_metadata, get_design_context, get_screenshot, download_assets), its platform-wide OAuth model, its per-seat tool-call quota, and the desktop-only/raster-scale rules already baked into the turn prompt. Use when a Figma link appears in chat, when deciding whether the Figma connector is even usable for this project, or when a Figma tool call fails and you need to tell a quota error from an auth error from "not enabled at all".

commands.name: skill:handling-mockup-image
commands.description: Read a static mockup image (a screenshot, hand sketch, or any flat PNG/JPG a chat message attached as a visual reference — never a live Figma file or an interactive Claude Design export) and map what it shows onto Core UI components when building or fixing a screen from it. Use whenever an attached image is the design source for a screen, not incidental data (a receipt, a bank statement, a photo to store); whenever a message carries TWO images (a screenshot of the screen as it is now plus the design it should match) and you must tell which is the target before changing anything; and whenever you need to verify a built screen against that reference image.

commands.name: skill:handling-pdf-specs
commands.description: Extract a spec, flow description, brand guideline, or screenshot export from a PDF a user attached in chat, using the four real MCP tools this repo now exposes over a local stdio server (`pdf-ingest`) — `inspect_ui_pdf`, `render_pdf_page`, `crop_pdf_region`, `extract_pdf_assets` — backed by a permissively-licensed default engine (`pypdfium2` + `pdfplumber`), with PyMuPDF selectable only behind explicit configuration for a deployment holding an Artifex commercial licence. Use whenever a chat attachment is a `.pdf`, before treating anything read from it as ground truth for layout or pixels. Falls back to the sandbox's `sips`+`tesseract` OCR workaround — page 1 only — only if the `pdf-ingest` MCP server is genuinely unavailable this turn.

commands.name: skill:migrating-legacy-mini-apps
commands.description: Rebuild a legacy mini app as a standard GG Studio Track C web mini app from its three real inputs — legacy source, a BRD or endpoint inventory, and a design source (Figma link, Claude Design export, mockup image or PDF) — so the result is complete on Core UI, calls its API through the Host runtime or sdk.http, and LOOKS like the design. Use when the input is an existing mini-app source tree, when deciding what to port and what to delete, when translating legacy HTTP / store / navigation / cross-app-global call sites, when reconciling three sources that disagree, or when reviewing a migration that compiles but does not match the design.

commands.name: skill:playwright-cli
commands.description: Automate browser interactions, test web pages and work with Playwright tests.

commands.name: skill:structuring-plan-documents
commands.description: What a GOOD GG Studio Plan Document looks like now that it is free-form Markdown with no fixed section list and no per-section gate -- the eight section names as default vocabulary rather than a quota, when a request earns phases and when it must not get any, why a stable R<n>/T<n> refId is worth keeping, what stays machine-readable (`tasks[]`/`phases[]`, `missing`) regardless of prose shape, and the real scaffold path convention (`src/pages/<screenId>.tsx`) a task's own `files` must declare against. Use when drafting or redrafting a Plan Document, when deciding which section names to use or whether a request needs phases at all, when unsure how many tasks belong in a phase, or when a drafted task's `files` names a screen or an App Definition location.

commands.name: skill:theming-galaxy-mini-apps
commands.description: Generate a mini app that FOLLOWS a brand at runtime instead of freezing one — the single brand/theme resolver, the `.gg-brand-<slug>` scope root, and the `?brand=hdbank` URL switch that repaints the whole app with no rebuild and no code change. Use when scaffolding or reviewing any generated app or screen, when a design has to be checked across the four brands or in dark theme, when a colour looks right in `vikki` and wrong elsewhere, or before claiming an app is brand-agnostic. Extracted and re-verified from `flight-booking-1`, the app where this mechanism actually works.

Use when a screen needs real customer data instead of a fixture, when migrating any legacy mini app, when a call returns 404 "no Route matched" or a 500 that is really a client mistake or a 200 that is actually a failure, or when deciding between a direct client now and sdk.http later.

commands.name: skill:debugging-galaxy-mini-apps
commands.description: Find the real cause of a defect in a generated mini app — a white screen on a route that compiles, a screen that renders while throwing, a total off by a tax nobody asked for, a guard that never refuses, a step that never advances, a call that returns 200 and shows nothing — and prove the fix in the running app rather than in the diff. Use when a turn opens with "The app you just built COMPILES but does not RUN", when the same error survives your fix, when a value on screen disagrees with the spec, when `tsc` and `vite build` are green and the preview is not, and before claiming any defect is fixed. Measured on real builds — 2,053 lines and a clean bundle hid a white screen, and one WebSocket line burned a whole repair turn on a defect never in `src/`.

commands.name: skill:enabling-miniapp-build-modes
commands.description: Make a GG Studio mini app ship all of its build modes — the ordinary Preview build (`dist/`), the single-file Standalone build (`dist-standalone/`, one `index.html` a reviewer double-clicks), the Host (mount) Module Federation manifest, and the Dual-thread engine build — so the Submit dialog's chips are live links instead of muted `· chưa bật` labels. Use when generating a new mini app, when a user asks for standalone/dual-thread/host support on an existing or legacy mini app, when a chip stays `chưa bật` after a submit, when a `standalone/` link opens a blank page, or before claiming a mode is enabled. Every rule here is read off the platform code that decides (`static_build.py`, `host_registry.py`, `submit_steps_router.py`) and was measured on a real build of this platform's own scaffold.

commands.name: skill:enforcing-spec-rules
commands.description: Turn a requirement document's stated rules — a deadline, a formula, a quantity, a set of named states — into code that actually refuses the wrong thing, and verify it by driving the app rather than by reading the diff. Use whenever a BRD, spec, or acceptance-criteria list states a number, a time limit, a total, or a list of statuses; whenever a screen shows a countdown, a price, a counter, or a result badge; and before claiming a requirement is implemented. This is the behavioural counterpart to the screenshot-compare-fix loop — that loop proves a screen LOOKS right, and nothing else in this skill set proves it BEHAVES right.

commands.name: skill:find-skills
commands.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

commands.name: skill:galaxy-app-definition
commands.description: Author a GG Studio App Definition (app-definition/ directory) from a mini app's real source code, so the Studio's Visual, Layout and Journey editors can render the app structurally. Read this after writing or changing screen code.

commands.name: skill:galaxy-core-ui
commands.description: Build UI with the GalaxyFinX Core UI design system (@galaxyfinx/galaxy-g-core-ui-web) so screens look native to the platform and survive every brand and theme. Use when writing or reviewing any screen, component, or styling for a GalaxyFinX host app or mini app (Vikki, HDBank, VietJet Air, Smile Living), when choosing which Core UI component to use, when a screen must work for more than one brand, or when a design looks hand-built instead of systemic. Also use before building a result, receipt, success, processing or failure screen — the platform's status mark is ReceiptCard's animated icon/confetti/logo slots, not Icon name="success", and a static design frame is not evidence against motion — and whenever a story's snippet passes an image path a turn is about to copy verbatim.

commands.name: skill:galaxy-frontend-sdk
commands.description: Call other mini apps and platform capabilities from a GalaxyFinX/Vikki mini app via the frontend SDK broker (@galaxyfinx/galaxy-g-frontend-sdk) and the HTTP client (@galaxyfinx/galaxy-g-http-client). Use when a mini app needs payment, eKYC, keychain, device id, or any capability another mini app or the Host provides, when wiring inter-mini-app calls, or when deciding whether an SDK feature works in a web Module Federation remote at all.

commands.name: skill:galaxy-miniapp-reference
commands.description: Real, verbatim reference source from `flight-booking-1` (the current gold-standard GG Studio-generated mini app) for the patterns a rule alone cannot teach — a real two-column responsive shell, a real sticky action bar, real measured breakpoints. Use when building a multi-step flow, a detail-plus-sidebar screen, or any screen that must behave correctly at both desktop and a real 390px phone width. Complements `building-galaxy-mini-apps` (rules) and `galaxy-core-ui` (component choice) — this skill is examples, not rules.

commands.name: skill:generating-miniapp-screens
commands.description: The ORDER a screen is generated in, and the reasoning at each step — inventory the design, derive the grid from the design system's own constants, place regions, pick components, wire mock data with real latency, then states, then colour and assets, then hover/motion, and measure after every step. Use when generating a new mini app or a new screen from any design source, when a generated screen compiles but looks hand-built or "almost right", when deciding what to build first, or when a fix keeps moving the layout instead of settling it.

commands.name: skill:handling-claude-design
commands.description: Read, drive, and describe a Claude Design export (a `*.dc.html` document plus its `_ds/`, `assets/`, `uploads/` siblings) cheaply and correctly when building a mini app from one. Use when a project's design source is a Claude Design export, when deciding what screens or variants it has, what a screen actually looks like, which design-system components map onto Core UI, or how to open one exact screen in a browser that has no click-through navigation to it.

commands.name: skill:handling-figma-design
commands.description: Build a GG Studio screen from a pasted Figma link using this repo's own Figma MCP integration (agent-service/app/mcp, doc 70) — the real, wired tool surface (get_metadata, get_design_context, get_screenshot, download_assets), its platform-wide OAuth model, its per-seat tool-call quota, and the desktop-only/raster-scale rules already baked into the turn prompt. Use when a Figma link appears in chat, when deciding whether the Figma connector is even usable for this project, or when a Figma tool call fails and you need to tell a quota error from an auth error from "not enabled at all".

commands.name: skill:handling-mockup-image
commands.description: Read a static mockup image (a screenshot, hand sketch, or any flat PNG/JPG a chat message attached as a visual reference — never a live Figma file or an interactive Claude Design export) and map what it shows onto Core UI components when building or fixing a screen from it. Use whenever an attached image is the design source for a screen, not incidental data (a receipt, a bank statement, a photo to store); whenever a message carries TWO images (a screenshot of the screen as it is now plus the design it should match) and you must tell which is the target before changing anything; and whenever you need to verify a built screen against that reference image.

commands.name: skill:handling-pdf-specs
commands.description: Extract a spec, flow description, brand guideline, or screenshot export from a PDF a user attached in chat, using the four real MCP tools this repo now exposes over a local stdio server (`pdf-ingest`) — `inspect_ui_pdf`, `render_pdf_page`, `crop_pdf_region`, `extract_pdf_assets` — backed by a permissively-licensed default engine (`pypdfium2` + `pdfplumber`), with PyMuPDF selectable only behind explicit configuration for a deployment holding an Artifex commercial licence. Use whenever a chat attachment is a `.pdf`, before treating anything read from it as ground truth for layout or pixels. Falls back to the sandbox's `sips`+`tesseract` OCR workaround — page 1 only — only if the `pdf-ingest` MCP server is genuinely unavailable this turn.

commands.name: skill:migrating-legacy-mini-apps
commands.description: Rebuild a legacy mini app as a standard GG Studio Track C web mini app from its three real inputs — legacy source, a BRD or endpoint inventory, and a design source (Figma link, Claude Design export, mockup image or PDF) — so the result is complete on Core UI, calls its API through the Host runtime or sdk.http, and LOOKS like the design. Use when the input is an existing mini-app source tree, when deciding what to port and what to delete, when translating legacy HTTP / store / navigation / cross-app-global call sites, when reconciling three sources that disagree, or when reviewing a migration that compiles but does not match the design.

commands.name: skill:playwright-cli
commands.description: Automate browser interactions, test web pages and work with Playwright tests.

commands.name: skill:structuring-plan-documents
commands.description: What a GOOD GG Studio Plan Document looks like now that it is free-form Markdown with no fixed section list and no per-section gate -- the eight section names as default vocabulary rather than a quota, when a request earns phases and when it must not get any, why a stable R<n>/T<n> refId is worth keeping, what stays machine-readable (`tasks[]`/`phases[]`, `missing`) regardless of prose shape, and the real scaffold path convention (`src/pages/<screenId>.tsx`) a task's own `files` must declare against. Use when drafting or redrafting a Plan Document, when deciding which section names to use or whether a request needs phases at all, when unsure how many tasks belong in a phase, or when a drafted task's `files` names a screen or an App Definition location.

commands.name: skill:theming-galaxy-mini-apps
commands.description: Generate a mini app that FOLLOWS a brand at runtime instead of freezing one — the single brand/theme resolver, the `.gg-brand-<slug>` scope root, and the `?brand=hdbank` URL switch that repaints the whole app with no rebuild and no code change. Use when scaffolding or reviewing any generated app or screen, when a design has to be checked across the four brands or in dark theme, when a colour looks right in `vikki` and wrong elsewhere, or before claiming an app is brand-agnostic. Extracted and re-verified from `flight-booking-1`, the app where this mechanism actually works.

commands.name: skill:wherdr
